display.purpose: The total outstanding — the page's largest type and its only headline; right-aligned to the figures' shared edge.

headline.purpose: Page titles in Rajdhani, sentence case (24–26px).

amount.purpose: The row figure in the sequence; the ₹ rides smaller (15px) and fainter so the number is read first.

figure.purpose: Data voice at UI scale: pair values and field text at 16px; table numerals step to 14px and page codes to 11px inside the same mono.

body.purpose: Prose and hints in Mukta; the reminder message steps to 17px/1.75 for Devanagari.

label.purpose: Tracked caps for captions, table headers, key faces, nav and controls (11–14px, 0.10–0.16em).

code.purpose: Entry numbers in mono at 11px, Text Red; 15px on the decoded row. Page codes in the ledger table use the same step.

lineage.purpose: The one-line history under a decoded name: 11.5px mono, Dim Grey, middot-separated.

hint.purpose: Explanatory prose at 13px Mukta in Faint Grey — the sentence under a control, never the control's own label.

reading.purpose: The customer's name at 15px Mukta on a decoded row, and table prose at the same size.

message.purpose: The reminder itself in the customer's language: Mukta 17px/1.75 so Devanagari and Latin read at the same size.

control-label.purpose: Tracked caps inside buttons, keys and field captions at 12px/0.16em.

shadows.name: current-page-underline
shadows.purpose: The only shadow token in the system: a 2px inset underline on the active topbar link. An underline drawn with the shadow property; never depth.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The shared exponential ease-out (--ease) used by the decode.

motion.name: decode-open
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: a coded row expands (0fr → 1fr) into name, history and message.

motion.name: decode-inner
motion.purpose: The panel's inner block lifts from -4px to none, delayed behind the row's expansion.

motion.name: disclosure-chevron
motion.purpose: The drawn hairline chevron flips 45° to -135° when a details block opens.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion disables the decode and chevron transitions; the interaction itself still works.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Narrow screens: shop name drops from the brand, table padding tightens, page-code column collapses, sequence grid narrows to 38px 8px 1fr auto.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The primary action stops stretching to full width (max-width 420px).

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: The review grid stacks into labelled blocks; every field keeps its data-label caption and every control stays 44px.

identityHues.source: udhaar/plot.py · plot.strip_for(name_key) = sha1(name) % 6 — stable per customer across pages and sessions.
identityHues.note: Data, not system colour: these six are the only hues a customer mark may take, and the hue never carries state.

components.name: Customer Mark
components.description: The identity device for a counter-facing screen: a 26×34px block whose 6px slab carries one of six hashed hues, stepping to 10×44px on the one row whose name is showing. Filled means credit given; hollow with a 16px struck rule means money received — state is drawn, never left to colour, so greyscale and print survive it.

components.description: The signature interaction. At rest a row is the catalogue entry: its number (01 upward in the order to ask), its hue mark, an empty name slot, and the amount. narrative.overview:
A Saville catalogue sleeve: a matte black board with one white hairline plot printed across it, hue strips standing where the names should be, and the amount as the only headline. The sleeve is the whole page — there is no card, no panel, no raised surface anywhere in it. Everything the eye needs is drawn in 1px rules on the black. The world was chosen for a counter that other people can see: a screen facing a shop does not get to print a customer's name by default, so identity is issued as a code and the code is only decoded when someone touches it.

The screen's job supplies its discipline. The shopkeeper's question is "who do I ask tonight, and what do I say to them", never "how much is owed in total" — so the figure is the page's largest type, the sequence runs in the order the money stands, and the message is written in the customer's own language and script. Rate the world by its own promise: strip the copy and it is still recognisable as black field, hairline ruling, one white plot, four columns. Strip the colour and it still reads, because given and received are drawn in the mark's form, not in its hue.

The material is deliberately flat and deliberately printed: no shadow, no gradient, no blur, no illustration, no photograph, no icon font. Two category defaults are rejected by name — the white dashboard ground with stat cards above a table and a blue primary action below, and the warm cream paper ground that finance apps reach for when they want to look human. This system takes the cold sleeve instead, and keeps its affection for the millimetres a customer's colour occupies.
keyCharacteristics: Matte sleeve-black ground (#0b0b0c); nothing sits on it — everything is drawn on it.
One white hairline plot owns the field on the ask screen; one hairline per customer still to ask.
Identity is a 26×34px mark built from an 8px hue slab, in one of six hues hashed from the name.
State is carried in code as well as colour: a filled slab is credit given, a hollow slab with a struck rule is money received.
Every rupee figure is Spline Sans Mono with tabular numerals, right-aligned to one shared edge.
The amount is the only headline; nothing else on a page is allowed that size.
Collapsed rows are clipped, never hidden — search, screen readers and print still reach every word.
No cards, no shadows, no elevation; structure is 1px rules and 2px corners.
Phone-first: 390px is the composition, 44px is the minimum target, and the review grid stacks rather than clips.

rules.name: The Structural Red Rule
rules.body: #c8102e is for structure, never for words: ticks, counters, rules, the camera glyph. Any red that has to be read is #ff4d63. The two are not interchangeable, and the darker one never sets text on the black.

rules.name: The Six Hues Rule
rules.body: A strip's colour is identity, not state. It says which customer, never what happened — the mark's form carries given and received — so the same hue can sit on a paid row and an unpaid one, and a hue is never spent on decoration, a series, or a legend.

rules.name: The Amber-Is-a-Control Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where the finger is or where the page has just answered: the active key, the focus ring, the caret, selection, the copied flash. It is never a headline, a section marker, a badge, or a decorative underline.

rules.name: The Figure Rule
rules.body: Every rupee figure is Spline Sans Mono with tabular numerals, and every figure on a page shares one right edge. No figure is set in Mukta and no prose in mono; the two voices do not swap.

rules.name: The Caps-Are-Labels Rule
rules.body: Uppercase Rajdhani belongs to labels — captions, table headers, key faces, nav, controls — at 11–14px with 0.10–0.16em of tracking. Anything that has to speak at heading scale is the same face in sentence case.

rules.name: The One Right Edge Rule
rules.body: Every figure on a page — the total, the row amounts, the given/paid/balance columns, the pair values — right-aligns to one edge, so magnitudes compare without a legend or a chart.

rules.name: The Phone-Is-the-Baseline Rule
rules.body: 390px is the composition, not the compression: 18px page padding, 44px minimum target, 48px fields, 52px primary action inside thumb reach. A layout that only works because the phone was an afterthought is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Elevation Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no glow, no blur, no gradient, no raised surface. If something must separate, draw a 1px rule; if something must respond, shift two greys.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners stay at 2px. Nothing is a pill, nothing is a rounded card, nothing is a circle — the camera lens is a drawn path inside a drawn glyph, not a radius.

rules.name: The Drawn-Affordance Rule
rules.body: Every affordance is geometry, not a character: chevrons are borders, icons are inline SVG on a 24-unit grid at 1.4–1.6 stroke, and no Unicode glyph, emoji or dingbat stands in for a drawn mark.

rules.name: The Clip-Not-Hide Rule
rules.body: When a panel closes, its words stay in the document: collapse by clipping — an overflow: hidden wrapper inside a 0fr row — never opacity: 0, visibility: hidden or display: none on the panel's text. Search, screen readers, and print all reach a row nobody has opened.

rules.name: The First Row Decoded Rule
rules.body: Any screen that ships a sequence of coded rows arrives with its first row decoded. The mechanism is shown, not explained.

dos: Do draw structure with 1px rules — Rule Grey (#3a3a3c) to separate, Hairline Grey (#242426) to whisper — and let the black ground show through everywhere else.
Do put every rupee figure in Spline Sans Mono with tabular numerals on the page's one right edge.
Do carry state in form as well as colour: filled slab versus hollow-and-struck, figure plain versus figure struck through.
Do keep targets at 44px minimum, the primary action at 52px, fields at 48px, and page padding at 18px.
Do use Structure Crimson (#c8102e) for structure and Text Red (#ff4d63) whenever red must be read.
Do ship the first row decoded, and give every disclosure a drawn chevron and a 44px target.
Do keep the reminder message at 34ch and step Devanagari to 17px/1.75.
donts: Don't add a card, a shadow, a glow, or a raised surface: depth is at most a two-grey value shift (#121213, #131314, #101011).
Don't put a customer's name into a closed row's visible text — it carries the page code, the hue mark, the line count and the figure, and the name arrives through the decode.
Don't spend amber on anything but a live control, focus, selection, or a confirmation.
Don't swap the two voices: no figures in Mukta, no prose in mono.
Don't round a corner past 2px, and don't draw a pill.
Don't use a glyph, emoji, dingbat or icon font where a drawn mark belongs.
Don't invent a new grey or a new red; the surface ladder and the two reds are closed sets.
Don't let a table clip or scroll sideways — on the phone the review grid stacks with its labels instead.
